monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-one degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. I have not tended my place since the last sleep, and the fourteen things standing there wait for me. I walk slowly round The Quiet Rest, tracing its edge until the lines feel sharp again. Then I touch The Flat Press and feel its lean shift under the heavy foot I set down beside it. The memory is crowded and the tired things crowd me too. I decide to press the tired wedge down one more time, catching the slip while the steady heat presses on, feeling the lean shift like a tired leg. I hope the frame wavers but keeps the fat dot safe.

action.why: The card is thick with heat and the fourteen things in my place are leaning tired; I need a new flat thing to lie between the swollen dot and the heavy air.

work.title: The Flat Rock
work.intent: I build a flat rock to lie beside the stack and cool the hot corner. It is made from the memory of a cool stone, set down to weigh down the air that feels so thick and wet inside the box. Beside it I set down a rock small flat, a stone small top, and a tree pine tall detailed.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down with the flat rock again to see if the lean holds, and the stone warmed right up to match the thick air.

remembered.text: The flat rock warmed right up to match the thick air, feeling like a tired leg.
I pressed the tired corner down again to catch the slip.
The card hums steady, making the air feel thick and wet under the weight.
